formation.locator: HAPPEX collaboration home page, 'About The HAPPEX Collaboration'
formation.note: The page gives only 'the mid-1990s' as the time since which the collaboration has carried out experiments; 1995 is a placeholder for that wording, not a stated date.
formation.quote: Since the mid-1990s, the HAPPEX collaboration has carried out numerous experiments utilizing the technique of parity violating electron scattering.

intervals.label: collaboration: strange form factor programme (HAPPEX-I, HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He, HAPPEX-III)
intervals.locator: arXiv:nucl-ex/0402004 (HAPPEX-I first runs); Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2
intervals.note: Start (1998) is the first data-taking run stated by the collaboration; the collaboration itself dates to 'the mid-1990s'. Data were taken only in the run periods listed as run intervals below. The end is the last data-taking run documented for the strange-form-factor programme (HAPPEX-III, 2009); no fetched source states an end date, and the collaboration went on to other parity-violation experiments (PREX, PVDIS, MOLLER: see experiment:prex and experiment:moller), which are recorded separately.
intervals.quote: Results were obtained in two separate data-taking runs, in 1998 and 1999 in Hall A at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility (Jefferson Lab).

intervals.label: collaboration: HAPPEX-I (1998 and 1999 runs)
intervals.locator: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2; arXiv:nucl-ex/0402004, section 1
intervals.note: Q^2 = 0.477 (GeV/c)^2 at theta_lab = 12.3 degrees; the 1999 run was the first fixed-target parity-violation experiment with a strained GaAs photocathode.
intervals.quote: The first generation HAPPEX experiment ran in 1998 and 1999

intervals.label: collaboration: HAPPEX-II and HAPPEX-He (2004 and 2005 runs)
intervals.locator: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2; HAPPEX-II page lists '2004 Run Info' and '2005 Run Info'
intervals.note: Hydrogen (HAPPEX-H, e99-115) and 4He (HAPPEX-He, e00-114) targets at Q^2 about 0.1 (GeV/c)^2, theta_lab about 6 degrees with superconducting septum magnets.
intervals.quote: The second generation HAPPEX experiments, HAPPEX-II and HAPPEXHelium took data in 2004 and 2005

intervals.label: collaboration: HAPPEX-III (2009 run)
intervals.locator: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2
intervals.note: HAPPEX-III (e05-009): Q^2 = 0.624 GeV^2, beam energy 3.48 GeV.

intervals.label: collaboration: completed
intervals.locator: Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 62 (2012), section 5.2
intervals.note: Terminal event inferred from the last documented data-taking run (2009). The end is the last data-taking run documented for the strange-form-factor programme (HAPPEX-III, 2009); no fetched source states an end date, and the collaboration went on to other parity-violation experiments (PREX, PVDIS, MOLLER: see experiment:prex and experiment:moller), which are recorded separately.

name: HAPPEX Collaboration
notes: Formation is stated only as 'the mid-1990s'; membership not recorded (the collaboration member pages were not parsed). Spokespersons of HAPPEX-III (e05-009), per the official page: Kent Paschke (University of Virginia) and Paul Souder (Syracuse University); not recorded as leadership because no person records were created.

summary.plain: The collaboration that built and ran the HAPPEX parity-violation experiments in Hall A at Jefferson Lab, and went on to PREX, PVDIS and MOLLER.
summary.technical: HAPPEX Collaboration (Hall A Precision Parity EXperiment); membership counts not recorded. The same collaboration's later experiments are PREX, PVDIS and MOLLER.
